2.9.3 Implementation Aspect
For the BSW service component this pattern means that operations of the same service interface might be called simultaneously on multiple partitions on the same- or even different cores. One precondition therefore is that service APIs are specified to be reentrant. This attribute applies to single core- multi-threaded systems and allows concurrent invocation of the operations by application SWCs on different tasks. If it is not given (Reentrancy = Non Reentrant), it must not be overridden by this pattern by allowing concurrent invocation of service interfaces by application SWCs on different partitions. Applying the pattern may also impact the runtime behavior of an API with respect to its "Sync/Async" attribute. A return of an synchronous API does not necessarily mean that the effect of the API has taken place but can also mean, that the API merely stored the function arguments and has triggered an internal processing request related to the API call. For example, the hypothetical API <MSN>_RequestState(x) is used to set the module’s internal state to ’x’. If now the API is invoked on a different partition, it is legit that <MSN> buffers ’x’ and performs the state change after the context has been switched back. Guide to BSW Distribution Callbacks of asynchronous APIs shall be invoked in the context of the same partition as the corresponding API. This means that a caller can remain unchanged, the BSW service needs to take care for performing any internal partition transitions. How a component handles the concurrent access in multiple partitions is completely implementation specific. A simple solution for the components is to use a SchM_Call(). However, since this is in the end the same mechanism as the RTE uses for core-transitions, such an implementation will not bring significant efficiency-benefits (latency, CPU overhead).
